partnershipPlan: Two older adult patient partners review the outcome definitions and the plain-language summary; a community pharmacist representative advises on refill behaviour; the geriatric medicine consultants review the covariate list before data access.
socialListening: No social media listening; the hospital's patient advice service summarises anonymised enquiries about medicines stopped at discharge from the last year.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: My bladder tablets let me sleep through the night; take them away and I am up four times, and that is when I would fall.
items.implication: Report benefits and harms together and treat night-time toileting as a competing fall risk when interpreting results.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Mum came home on a new tablet for her mood and was muddled for a week before anyone connected the two.
items.implication: Keep the new-user analysis in the first 30 days as a pre-specified question.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: If we review everyone over 70 we will do nothing else on the discharge list, so I need to know it is worth it.
items.implication: Frame a precise null result as a useful answer that frees pharmacist time.

items.theme: What happens after the first month
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Half the medicines on a discharge list have changed by the time the first repeat prescription comes to us.
items.implication: Treat exposure after 30 days as uncertain and report the 30-day window.

summary: Four composite voices on benefit, new starts, workload and exposure drift.
